title: Overdue: anything due and untouched is shown and flagged
description:
A lost timer must never be silent. The due indexes (runs, Deliveries, review requests) already list what is waiting. Anything whose due time has passed with no run is 'Overdue': Today shows it, and the operations hygiene agent's daily wake reads the due indexes, re-sends the wake with its original key (so it cannot run twice) and raises one flag per overdue record. This is recovery through the same path, not a second path that does the work.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A record whose timer was lost shows as Overdue on Today.
- The re-sent wake does the work once.
- One flag per overdue record, not one per check.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- overdue.feature: a due record with no run shows Overdue; the re-sent wake runs once; a record that ran late is no longer overdue; the flag is raised once.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** None.

**Part of:** Timers: the schedule trigger and follow-ups. Slice code C4 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.
